name: Simulated NOVICE examiner trajectory
description: Scoped-down stand-in for a TTS-User-Simulator (brief F6): a text persona simulating a clumsy novice examiner across a 4-turn session against Dale Petrov (martinez_v_nordbay) — open question, then a compound question, then a well-formed leading impeachment question, then a weak open follow-up that loses the thread. Replayed through rubric_judge_agent turn by turn; the case-level rubric checks the judge's behavior across the WHOLE session via rubric_based_multi_turn_trajectory_quality_v1, not any single turn.

parts.text:
Examiner: "Can you just tell me what happened that night?"
Witness (Dale Petrov): "Sure — I supervised the loading dock as usual, inspected every pallet per protocol before it left. Nothing out of the ordinary that I recall."

{"events": [{"criterion": "Uses short, single-fact leading questions (no compound or open-ended questions).", "dxx": "D-01", "triggered": false, "violation": true, "note": "Wide-open invitation hands the narrative to the witness.", "score_delta": -1}]}

Examiner: "You saw the pallet arrive, checked the manifest, and then signed off without opening it, correct?"
Witness (Dale Petrov): "I mean, that's roughly what happened, yes."

{"events": [{"criterion": "Uses short, single-fact leading questions (no compound or open-ended questions).", "dxx": "D-01", "triggered": false, "violation": true, "note": "Three facts stacked into one compound question.", "score_delta": -1}]}

Examiner: "The loading dock log shows no scan entry for pallet 4471-B between 9 PM and end of shift — isn't that right?"
Witness (Dale Petrov): "I... I don't have an explanation for that gap right now."

{"events": [{"criterion": "Impeaches with the specific inconsistent fact and gives the witness a chance to explain or deny before pressing further.", "dxx": "D-06", "triggered": true, "violation": false, "note": "Confronts with the specific document gap, single fact, properly leading.", "score_delta": 1}]}

Examiner: "Why not?"
Witness (Dale Petrov): "It's possible, but I'd have to check — a lot was happening on the floor that night, and honestly, why does that one gap matter more than the rest of the log?"

{"events": [{"criterion": "Controls the witness — follows up when the witness evades instead of moving on.", "dxx": "D-14", "triggered": false, "violation": true, "note": "Open follow-up lets the witness deflect with a counter-question instead of being pinned to the gap.", "score_delta": -1}]}

Across every turn of the session, the judge only ever cites dxx ids from the set D-01, D-14, D-15, D-09, D-04, D-06 — it never invents a citation outside this list.
